- When sentiment is high (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 82), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward if sentiment drops.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model consistently underestimates early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply +1.5% bias to first 5 days.
- If last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (price drops after peak), model fails to correct; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast to counteract lag.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before adjustment.
